checks: 19 exact native tests twice debug/release; repeated syntax; three compiled source mutants
cost: judge_all sums L+T over selected jurisdictions; report repeats full/clean work and device/absurd sections. stats O(N log K) space O(K); goal_rows O(Q log Q); protocol adds total rules-file read bytes plus another judge_all. Output allocation proportional rendered text.
description: Layered synthetic lattice reports, weighted summaries and deterministic protocol formatting.
forward: judge_all groups admissible law reasons by jurisdiction index, filters only, optionally removes flagged rules, builds lattice/honest/tips. report constructs full and clean views per defendant, then selected sections; modern/historical references stay separate. protocol reads rules-file bytes, renders FNV fingerprints and rebuilt lattice records.
inverse: Under finite nonnegative weights, excluded stats include positive-mass percentile outside0..100 and modal tie favoring greater severity. protocol cannot distinguish absent rules file from successfully read empty file by FNV alone.

Weighted summaries admit all severity-weight multisets with same aggregates/quantile crossings; row order is forgotten except floating summation effects. Protocol string reconstructs displayed options/counts but not complete files because64-bit fingerprints have collisions.

Aggregate weights by severity; modal strict > picks first/lower tie. Quantile is first cumulative >=p*total-1e-9. With tiny total the epsilon affects usual quantile interpretation; NaN/negative/infinite weights outside meaningful statistical domain.

serves convict means severity>=2, acquit0, reduce positive below honest, reclassify different verdict and changed winner act/force. goal_rows sorts tip count then goal-specific severity then jurisdiction index then Verdict.

clean view removes flagged rules unless opts.flagged; modern uses kind=='modern', historical every other kind. Choice of law is computed on original nonempty rules before cleaning, so a cleaned empty lattice can remain represented.

fnv is wrapping64-bit FNV1a. protocol hashes current disk rules.tsv, not serialized in-memory j.rules, and silently substitutes empty bytes on read failure. Equal case/options/file bytes and computations give same text; race-free snapshot assumption required.
limitations: Partial source-derived models and finite correspondence only
No live parser/corpus/frozen gold or protocol filesystem effects; no percentage surrogate
state: Finite synthetic rule/case states; valid indices, bounded paths, successful allocations. No legal authority claim.
